title: Accelerated Spatio-Temporal Bayesian Modeling for Multivariate Gaussian Processes
problem: Multivariate Gaussian processes offer powerful probabilistic modeling for complex interdependent phenomena but pose significant computational challenges in high-dimensional spatio-temporal settings.
motivation: Scientific applications require scalable Bayesian inference on large spatio-temporal datasets. Current methods lack sufficient performance for real-world data volumes and spatial resolutions.
method: DALIA speeds up inference for multivariate Gaussian processes (systems with many interconnected variables where predictions are correlated) using graphics processors (GPUs) and a mathematical shortcut called integrated nested Laplace approximation (INLA), which trades some accuracy for much faster calculation. The method stores model relationships as sparse inverse covariance matrices—keeping only important connections rather than dense full matrices—and organizes these into block-dense chunks for efficient GPU processing. Work is distributed across multiple computers in a hierarchy using distributed-memory parallelism, so different machines can solve different pieces of the problem simultaneously.
key_novelty: Combining GPU acceleration with hierarchical distributed parallelism enables INLA to handle multivariate Gaussian processes efficiently across hundreds of supercomputer nodes.
contributions: DALIA framework for scalable multivariate GP Bayesian inference
Application: 48-day air pollution study at refined spatial resolution
limitations: Evaluation limited to air pollution case study; INLA approximations may not suit all GP applications; scalability beyond 496 nodes not demonstrated.
